row.body_md: Formal verification decision (2026-11-25). Goals: find design bugs early and prevent invariant regressions. Friction: path-filtered PR job plus a deeper nightly; a failing model blocks release only for properties modeled at that release. v0.1.0 is blocked only by models that exist then (claim and parser proofs); schedule/async/delivery/reveal models are required before 1.0. Stack: TLA+/TLC, proptest-state-machine against the real engine, and Kani for parsers and custom IDs. First model: claim/offer/custody/expiry with a bounded logical clock and per-pair deadlines. Per-model runtime ceilings: 5 minutes on PR, 20 minutes nightly; if exceeded, reduce scope or use Apalache, never silently skip. Conformance: shared action vocabulary plus real-engine proptests; Tier 3 uses ITF replay after a spike, with NDJSON trace validation as fallback. Anonymity: projection tests, canary strings, outbound-effect audit, and log scans, not a TLA+ proof. Human owns property meaning; agents may update specs for mechanical drift. Every property must have a deliberately broken mutation that fails. Tools are pinned by checksum; the jar is not committed. Formal artifacts are dev-only, have zero product dependency, and can be deleted in one PR. Scripts are authoritative; the project-local skill is optional guidance. Formal checks are not architecture drivers. Coverage target: feature-aligned modules (Claim, Schedule, Async, Delivery, Reveal), then maintain; no open-ended expansion. No fixed maintenance budget, but a per-model runtime ceiling and a tracked waiver process prevent the program from becoming a hurdle. Full research and rationale: to be recorded in docs/FORMAL_METHODS.md when implementation starts.

Adopt none as a runtime dependency. Use the MIT best practices in a project-local skill after the spike; scripts and CI remain authoritative. Key pitfalls to guard: spec drift (record sync commits and map actions), vacuous properties (mandatory mutation), state explosion (small scopes and runtime ceilings), bounded-check complacency (state assumptions), and anonymity claims that TLA+ cannot support (use projection tests).

row.body_md: Scheduler algorithm scope: (1) randomized cyclic Latin square: build the canonical cyclic square, then permute rows (rounds), columns (tracks), and symbols (participants) with the event seed; (2) seeded row-by-row perfect matching, the current fallback; (3) balanced matching: min-cost max-flow with costs for repeated handoff pairs, recent encounters, uneven track exposure, and an own-track/seen-pair infeasible edge; (4) local-search improvement: swap two participants within a round only when both assignments stay valid and the balance metric improves; (5) repair: backtracking or min-cost flow with a Hall violator certificate, never relaxing no-repeat or own-track; (6) group rotation: split balanced groups, tracks stay in the original group, rotate people each K phases, fall back to the global pool for an infeasible phase, and log the repair; (7) balance metrics: max/min track exposure per participant, repeated handoff pairs, cross-group handoffs, group size ratio, and phase count. All strategies are deterministic for the same canonical input and seed. Strategy is selectable, default balanced. The demo matrix must use a seeded plan, not a cyclic shift.

row.body_md: Implementation plan for the delivery loop. Add a durable delivery outbox with a unique dedupe key per effect and a status of pending, sent, or failed. Store file bytes in the blob store and keep only the SHA-256 and storage path in the outbox row. Enqueue effects in the same transaction as the state change where possible. Send receipts through the same outbox. Use the dm_cursors table for backfill after downtime. If a DM is closed, send a host alert and use a host-approved private thread when configured; never fall back to a public channel.
